goal: Repair three migration-author-lane tooling defects in one coherent change: refuse a second issue reference in a claim title at --claim time (#2448 part 2), compare sorted --objects against sorted admitted writes in the post-mutex re-proof (#3125), and accept an already-applied version's original claim-head preview apply when the caller proves that head (#2491). No safety gate is weakened, disabled or bypassed.
dispatcher: Owner Albert Hazan authorized resolving all open non-orchestrator issues in this repository to production
prohibited_actions: No database write, migration, schema, function, view, role, grant or index change.
No production database command, no terraform or terragrunt apply, no mutating production gcloud.
Do not release, expire, reassign or otherwise mutate any live author claim, including claim #2745.
Do not disable, bypass or weaken any safety gate to make this change pass.
assumptions: Issue #2448 part 1 (the hard-coded expiry-sweep close comment) is already repaired on main by CLAIM_CLOSE_REASONS; only part 2 remains and only part 2 is changed here.

Issue #3117's remaining ask, a guarded worktree-rebind path in the lane tool, already exists on main as --rebind-claim-worktree (issue #3182) with nine passing guard tests; it is verified here, not reimplemented.
The preview-apply workflow names its instance binding's appliedCommit and its preview-migration-apply-<sha> artifact after the commit it checked out, so #2491 is repaired on the reader side only.
stop_conditions: Stop if any repair would require a database schema change; route it to the shared-db orchestrator instead.
Stop if a regression test cannot be shown to fail against the unfixed script.
